raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Balancing Summarization and Change Detection in Graph Streams
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Proposes a quantitative methodology to balance graph summarization and change detection in graph streams, using a hierarchical latent variable model and MDL principle to design parameterized summary graphs for temporal/streaming graphs.
overlaps: Applies graph summarization to compress large-scale graphs
Models graphs as sequences over time
differences: Uses MDL-based probabilistic hierarchical latent variable model for summarization, not graph autoencoder
Focuses on change detection accuracy, not representation learning for downstream tasks
Does not use RNN to learn temporal features
Does not train node representations via reconstruction error

sources.title: Balancing Summarization and Change Detection in Graph Streams
sources.quote: Graph summarization compresses large-scale graphs into a smaller scale. However, the question remains: To what extent should the original graph be compressed? This problem is solved from the perspective of graph change detection, aiming to detect statistically significant changes using a stream of summary graphs.

sources.title: Balancing Summarization and Change Detection in Graph Streams
sources.quote: We introduce a probabilistic structure of hierarchical latent variable model into a graph, thereby designing a parameterized summary graph on the basis of the minimum description length principle.

raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: A survey of graph summarization methods, covering clustering, compression, sampling, and influence detection approaches for condensing graphs into compact representations.
overlaps: Graph summarization as a method to compress graphs into more compact representations
differences: Survey of summarization techniques, not a representation learning method
Does not combine graph summarization with graph autoencoder or RNN
Does not address sequential/temporal graph representation learning

sources.title: Graph Summarization
sources.quote: One method for condensing and simplifying such datasets is graph summarization. It denotes a series of application-specific algorithms designed to transform graphs into more compact representations while preserving structural patterns, query answers, or specific property distributions.

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: kMatrix: A Space Efficient Streaming Graph Summarization Technique
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Proposes kMatrix, a memory-efficient streaming graph summarization technique that partitions allocated memory using a sample of the original graph stream.
overlaps: Graph summarization applied to streaming/temporal graphs
differences: Focuses on memory efficiency for query approximation, not representation learning
Does not use graph autoencoder or RNN
Does not generate fixed-size new graphs for downstream GNN/RNN training

sources.title: kMatrix: A Space Efficient Streaming Graph Summarization Technique
sources.quote: Many of these data streams are mapped into graphs, which helps discover some of their properties. However, due to the difficulty in processing massive streaming graphs, they are summarized such that their properties can be approximately evaluated using the summaries.

raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Studies the problem of producing summaries of multi-relation networks, where multiple edges of different types may exist between any pair of nodes, including temporal graph snapshots as a relation type.
overlaps: Graph summarization as a compression technique
Mentions temporal graph snapshots as a relation type
differences: Focuses on multi-relation graph summarization, not representation learning
Does not use graph autoencoder or RNN
Does not generate fixed-size graphs for GNN/RNN training

sources.title: Multi-relation Graph Summarization
sources.quote: Multi-relation graphs are an expressive model of real-world activities, in which a relation can be a topic in social networks, an interaction type in genetic networks, or a snapshot in temporal graphs.
